analysis.title: Your computer
analysis.intro: A read-only look at what this PC is and whether the tuning can be applied. Nothing is changed here.
opt.title: Choose what to optimize
opt.intro: Every optimization is explained before it runs, backed up, and can be undone from Restore.
opt.cpu.title: CPU thermal tuning
opt.cpu.desc: Undervolt, boost caps and power limits through ThrottleStop, applied at every logon, so the CPU stops hitting 100 °C.
opt.planned.power.title: Power plan
opt.planned.power.desc: Pick the Windows power plan and CPU boost mode that match your tuning.
opt.planned.services.title: Background services
opt.planned.services.desc: Pause non-essential services and startup apps while you play.
opt.planned.network.title: Network latency
opt.planned.network.desc: Reduce network lag with reversible adapter and DNS settings.
opt.planned.games.title: In-game settings
wizard.vbsCheckbox: Yes, disable VBS/hypervisor (required for the undervolt)
step.detect.title: Detect your hardware
step.detect.desc: Reads your operating system, CPU and laptop model. The tuning values are specific to the Intel Core i9-14900HX, so the app refuses to continue on any other CPU.
step.detect.c1: Nothing is changed in this step.
step.backup.title: Back up current settings
step.backup.desc: Saves a timestamped copy of ThrottleStop.ini so you can always return to where you started.
step.backup.c1: Creates ThrottleStop.ini.bak_<date> next to the ini (skipped on a fresh install).
step.get.title: Get ThrottleStop
step.get.desc: Uses the ThrottleStop you already have (the folder of your startup task, or one extracted in Downloads, Desktop or Documents). Otherwise it unpacks the zip (tested with 9.7.3) into the install folder: download it from TechPowerUp first and keep it in Downloads, or pick it manually.
step.get.c1: Extracts the zip to C:\Tools\ThrottleStop (or the folder you chose).
step.vbs.title: Turn off VBS / hypervisor
step.vbs.desc: ThrottleStop can only change CPU voltages while Windows virtualization-based security is off. This is a security setting, so it is your choice.
step.vbs.c1: bcdedit hypervisorlaunchtype off, VBS off, memory integrity off.
step.vbs.c2: Breaks WSL2 and Docker (WSL2) until you roll back.
step.vbs.c3: Needs a reboot to take effect.
step.apply.title: Apply the tuning
step.apply.desc: Writes the tested profile into ThrottleStop.ini.
step.apply.c1: Undervolt: -100 mV core and P-cache, -90 mV E-cache.
step.apply.c2: Boost caps: P-cores 47x (4.7 GHz), E-cores 36x (3.6 GHz).
step.apply.c3: Power limits: PL1 65 W / PL2 85 W.
step.task.title: Always-on startup
step.task.desc: Registers a Windows scheduled task so ThrottleStop starts at every logon and a 5-minute watchdog brings it back if it is closed. It never starts a second copy.
step.task.c1: Task "ThrottleStop_Autostart", highest privileges, no battery limits.
step.task.c2: Starts ThrottleStop now and remembers your Windows build for the Dashboard check.
step.verify.title: Verify
step.verify.desc: Compares the saved settings with the profile and checks that ThrottleStop, the task and the hypervisor setting are in the expected state.
step.verify.c1: Read-only. If VBS was just disabled, reboot first and run this again.
finish.title: All steps finished
finish.reboot: Reboot Windows once so the VBS change takes effect, then open this app again: the Dashboard will tell you whether everything is in place. After that, ThrottleStop starts by itself at every logon.
finish.ok: ThrottleStop starts by itself at every logon and the watchdog keeps it running. Open the Dashboard any time (for example after a Windows update) to check that the optimization is still in place.
restore.title: Undo everything
restore.intro: Put the PC back the way it was before the tuning.
restore.w1: Removes the always-on startup task (ThrottleStop stops being started for you).
restore.w2: Restores the newest ThrottleStop.ini.bak_* backup, undoing the undervolt, boost caps and power limits.
restore.w3: Optionally re-enables virtualization-based security so WSL2 and Docker work again (needs a reboot; the undervolt stops working).
restore.confirm: Remove the autostart task and restore the newest ThrottleStop.ini backup?
help.title: Questions
help.intro: Short answers. The full documentation has the details.
help.a1: Only ThrottleStop's profile (undervolt, boost caps, power limits), a startup task for ThrottleStop and, if you choose, the VBS/hypervisor setting. It does not touch game files.
help.a2: Every change is backed up and reversible from Restore. Still, changing CPU voltages can cause instability: this chip logged a corrected CPU error at −100 mV, so the app never goes deeper.
help.q3: Do I have to keep the app open?
help.a3: No. ThrottleStop starts at every logon and a 5-minute watchdog keeps it running. The app itself can stay in the system tray and re-check every few minutes.
help.q4: Why does it ask to turn VBS off?
help.a4: Windows blocks voltage changes while virtualization-based security is on. Turning it off is a security trade-off and breaks WSL2/Docker until you restore it.
help.q5: Will it work on my laptop?
help.a5: The CPU tuning values are specific to the Lenovo Legion 83DE with an i9-14900HX. On another CPU the app explains why it will not apply them.
settings.title: Preferences

settings.autostart: Start with the system (hidden in the tray)

settings.closeToTray: Closing the window keeps the app running in the tray
settings.notifications: Notify me when the optimization breaks
settings.installDir.hint: Leave empty to find it automatically (startup task, Downloads, Desktop, Documents).

settings.resetConfirm: Reset every setting to its default?
settings.adminNeeded: Changing this needs administrator rights. Restart the app as administrator.

msg.backup.none: Nothing to back up yet (fresh install).
msg.vbs.disabled: VBS/hypervisor disabled. Reboot required (also switch Memory integrity off in Windows Security).
msg.vbs.unchanged: Left unchanged. If the voltage controls stay locked, run this step again with VBS disabled.

msg.health.fail: The optimization is not fully in place.
